context: A teacher and student discuss a paper on infrastructure
purpose: Teach: 模擬/移入/膨張/大久保/重点的/流域/妨げる/動力

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、模擬実験、丁寧でしたね。
lines.en: Your paper and simulations were really thorough.
lines.style: Warm approval, slight lean forward. Genuine interest in the work. Steady pace, clear enunciation on 「丁寧」. Not rushed — she's reading the student carefully.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。外来種の移入が、生態系に及ぼす影響、論じました。
lines.en: Yes. I focused on how invasive species transfers affect ecosystem health.
lines.style: Respectful, careful articulation. Slight nervous energy underneath — wanting to get the scope right. Deliberate on technical terms. Eyes steady but not quite meeting hers.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 人口の膨張も、地域差が出ていますね。
lines.en: And you've really captured the regional variation in population patterns too.
lines.style: Thoughtful nod in the voice. Recognition that he's seeing the connections. Warm but observational — she's checking his depth of understanding. Slight pause before 「地域差」.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 大久保地区の事例、重点的に取り上げました。
lines.en: I went into detail with case studies from the Okubo district.
lines.style: Bit more confident here — he knows this part well. Crisp delivery on the place name. Slight lift at the end, inviting her to see why that choice mattered.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 河川流域の調査、川の生物多様性を妨げる要因、扱っていますね。
lines.en: You've handled the river-basin survey well — the factors that compromise biodiversity are clear.
lines.style: Reflective, almost thinking aloud. Not praising perfection, but recognizing genuine engagement with complexity. Warm and steady. Slight pause for breath after the dash.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 動力源の選択、政策に与えた影響、別章で論じます。
lines.en: I'm exploring energy-source choices and their policy implications in a separate chapter.
lines.style: Quiet lift of anticipation at the end. He's thought ahead. Respectful, organized tone. Slight exhale before the final phrase — this is the next piece he wants to tackle.
